source: Hacker's Delight, 2nd ed. (H. S. Warren), section 2-1 "Manipulating Rightmost Bits"
description: Next higher number with the same number of 1 bits (snoob, Gosper's hack)
notes: Same idea as Bit Twiddling Hacks #NextBitPermutation; function written by us from the idea. clang trunk -O3 -march=skylake already replaces the division by the lowest set bit with a shift by cttz: 9 IR instructions (sub, and, add, xor, lshr 2, cttz, lshr, or, ret); x86: blsi, add, mov, xor, shr, tzcnt, shrx, or. Division by zero at x = 0 is UB in the source. Re-checked 2026-10-28 to decide between A and C: no shorter correct form found by hand. Merging the two shifts into lshr by cttz(x) + 2 is rejected by Alive2 (poison at x = 0x40000000), and the x & ~r variant is rejected (value mismatch at x = 0xffffffff, where x + s wraps to 0). Settled 2026-10-29 with the reference toolchain: same 9 IR instructions as godbolt; LLM Compiler's 5 attempts (results/llmc-full-az4) found one proven body, not faster. Optimality is not established, so the entry stays in C.
